issues.description: The template's Bitmap24 class header declares the constructors, destructor and the methods (resize_buffer, save, set) under the private: section, while the program (main.cpp) and the solution expect to call these methods from outside the class. The solution's Bitmap24.hpp marks these members public. As-is, the template's visibility makes calls such as bitmap.resize_buffer(...) and bitmap.set(...) in main.cpp illegal and will prevent successful compilation, confusing students who follow the provided example usage.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the API used by main() public in the template header. Concretely, in example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp move or change the access specifier so that the constructors, destructor and the methods resize_buffer, save and set are declared under public: (matching the solution). Alternatively, keep width/height/data private but declare the constructors and the methods used by main() as public. This will restore compatibility with main.cpp and avoid compilation errors while preserving the intended exercise.
